# 2 Chronicles Chapter 21 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Jehoshaphat rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David. His son Jehoram succeeded him as king.

**2** Jehoram's brothers — the sons of Jehoshaphat — were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All were sons of King Jehoshaphat of Israel.

**3** Their father had given them generous gifts of silver, gold, and valuables, along with fortified cities in Judah. But the kingdom went to Jehoram because he was the firstborn.

**4** When Jehoram had established himself as king, he murdered all his brothers with the sword, along with some of the princes of Israel.

**5** Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

**6** He followed the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, because he had married Ahab's daughter. He did evil in the LORD's eyes.

**7** Nevertheless, the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David because of the covenant He had made with David, and because He had promised to maintain a lamp for him and his descendants forever.

**8** During Jehoram's reign, Edom rebelled against Judah and set up their own king.

**9** Jehoram crossed into Edom with his officers and all his chariots. He attacked by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him, along with his chariot commanders.

**10** To this day Edom has been in rebellion against Judah. Libnah revolted at the same time, because Jehoram had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.

**11** He also built high places in the hills of Judah and led the people of Jerusalem into unfaithfulness, leading Judah astray.

**12** A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying: "This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says: 'You have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or of Asa king of Judah.

**13** Instead, you have followed the ways of the kings of Israel. You have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem into unfaithfulness, just as the house of Ahab did. You have also murdered your own brothers — members of your own family — men who were better than you.

**14** So now the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives, and everything you own with a heavy blow.

**15** You yourself will be very ill with a lingering disease of the bowels, until the disease causes your bowels to come out, day after day.'"

**16** The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the hostility of the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Cushites.

**17** They attacked Judah, invaded it, and carried off all the property found in the royal palace, including his sons and wives. No son was left to him except Ahaziah, the youngest.

**18** After all this, the LORD struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels.

**19** Over time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in terrible pain. His people did not make a funeral fire in his honor, as they had for his ancestors.

**20** He was thirty-two when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He passed away, to no one's regret, and was buried in the City of David — but not in the royal tombs.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **21:4**: He murdered all his brothers. The man who was given everything — firstborn status, the kingdom, his father's legacy — destroyed his own family to feel secure. This is what happens when Ahab's values enter David's house.

- **21:7**: Even now, God doesn't destroy the dynasty. Not because Jehoram deserves mercy, but because David's covenant still stands. The lamp flickers but doesn't go out.

- **21:20**: "He passed away, to no one's regret." Six words, and they say everything. No fire, no royal tomb, no grief. He lived badly and died unmourned. The Chronicler doesn't editorialize — he doesn't need to.


— PNEUMA
